newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold Q1 profit seen up 75 percent.
newsitem.headline: Ahold Q1 profit seen up 75 percent.

text.p: Dutch supermarket chain Ahold is expected to post a hefty 75 percent increase in first quarter 1997 profits, as last year's U.S. acquisition Stop & Shop and a higher dollar boost U.S. income, analysts said.

Ahold on Thursday should report net profits from ordinary activities before preference dividends of some 240 million guilders from 138 million a year ago, they said. Estimates ranged from 227-255 million guilders.

One analyst, Arie Gravendeel of IRIS warned there could be a strong increase in interest payments incurred by the company's global expansion. He pencilled in 109 million guilders in interest charges, up from last year's 75 million.
"Taxes will also be on the rise, almost doubling to some 97 million guilders from 52 million one year ago," he said.
Others focused on the likely U.S. contribution to results.
"There are some very positive sounds coming from the U.S.," said Jurgen Veenker, analyst at MeesPierson.

He expected the $2.9 bilion acquisition to have boosted margins, and combined with the reorganisation programme "Project Compete", U.S. margins should be up to 3.9 percent from 2.4 percent in the first quarter of last year.
"And this year's first quarter also includes (high margin) New Year sales, as it started on December 30," he added.
This year, Ahold's first quarter figures include New Year's eve, while the year-ago period started on January 3, 1996.
In May, Ahold said U.S. sales had risen 53.9 percent to $4.2 billion during the first quarter. It said a strong dollar had boosted first quarter sales growth by 9.8 percent.
Analysts were also positive over developments within Ahold's domestic market as well.
"I expect ongoing efficiency improvements, higher productivity and extended store hours to have led to a margin increase to some 3.3 from 3.1 percent in the Netherlands, Gravendeel said.
Most Albert Heijn stores are now open until 2000 local time, with many open until ten and on Sundays as well.
Ahold has said 1997 first quarter sales in the Netherlands rose 6.1 percent to 4.7 billion guilders.
In spite of a previously-announced 32.1 percent increase in turnover in the rest of Europe to 639 million guilders, analysts foresee only muted profit growth in that area.

"I foresee some start-up losses in Poland and Spain, and margin pressure due to increased competition in Portugal," said Veenker, who expects non-Dutch European operating profit growth to be close to five percent in the first quarter.
Analysts were split on the contribution to profit of last November's Brazilian acquisition Bompreco.
"Operating income should amount to some eight million guilders over the first quarter in Brazil," said ING Barings' analyst Dennis Jullens.
Gravendeel said he expected Brazil to break even, adding that the cost of investments in Latin America had probably soaked up any gains.
Turnover generated in Brazil amounted to 474 million guilders in the first quarter, Ahold said in May.
First quarter turnover in the Asia Pacific region amounted to 274 million guilders in the first quarter, but analysts expected start-up costs to incur losses of between 15 and 20 million guilders.
"I expect the Asia Pacific region to turn break-even somewhere in 1999," said Veenker.
